schema: Documented departures for the reviewed v13 source, 2 Oct 2026.

p1.reason: Complete handoff experiment below the seven-step workflow. v13.10 (EO review): the right side of the figure, which repeated panel 4's handover stack, now prints B's other outcomes on the same trials, aligned with the lanes (acted on + declined + used the genuine record = trials); the take line gives the comparison on the 23 items every condition shares; the scope states the treatment (the emem lane adds a verifier and an instruction, so the figure tests the workflow) and the exploratory agent run of the matched baseline; the deterministic matched ablation (4 Oct: 23, 8, 3 and 0 of 23 corruptions accepted) is a labelled strip under the figure. A 17 pt line states the orbit design and its reference-harness scope.

p2.reason: The eight-value diagnostic replaces the dated NDVI history at the same print scale. Its choices connect the agent handoff to the central source-read experiment.

p3.reason: The conceptual change decomposition stays on one line with its scope caption. 4 Oct 2026: the drift-score figure leaves the face (both reviews rated it weakest; it is an uncalibrated heuristic), so panel 3 is short and the left column gives the space to panel 7's table and the full trace.

questions.reason: The eight memory operations retain their EO task labels and implemented single-hop scope. Future-work prose and a unit-test count leave the poster face. v13.10: moved to the right column after the memory model (panel 9), whose operations it lists; the left column takes the recovered full trace.

p4.reason: The decoded evidence object replaces the Berlin fanout, restoring the complete source-record-address-attestation flow at 396 by 98 mm.

p5.reason: The central mutation matrix keeps its 396 by 196 mm print size and measured outcomes. 4 Oct 2026: it follows the source-pixel panel at the foot of the centre column and is numbered 6.

p6.reason: The source-pixel experiment keeps its 396 by 128 mm figure and data. 4 Oct 2026 (two reviews): it moves above the mutation matrix, to eye level, and is numbered 5; both reviewers named it the strongest result.

p12.reason: v13.9 removes repeated prose and the redundant four-label bridge, reducing this band from 147.5 to 91.5 mm. All 33 retained community labels keep their wording and font sizes. Cards are rearranged beside a dedicated 50 mm Connect QR; the measured 11-path / 9-signature result remains. v13.10 (issue #58): the five primary cards quote each listing's own words (ChatGPT, Claude directory, Dify Marketplace, GitHub MCP Registry, ClawHub), verbatim from the authors' screenshots, which are kept in research/v13/evidence/listings/ but not printed (their text sets at about 5 pt at A0). VS Code and MuleSoft Exchange move into the lists, which print two lines per group.

p13.reason: The contribution remains in the left column, after the consolidated evidence boundary.

footer.reason: The brief's footer text is three lines at 14 pt over 801 mm (line 2 alone is about 560 characters), plus the F12 credit line: 18 mm from 1169.5 mm (brief 13 mm from 1172).

p7.reason: The checkable/not-established table is consolidated on the left. It includes the former threat-model scope. The duplicated right-column section 7 is removed.

p8.reason: The right column begins with temporal memory after the duplicated boundary panel is removed. The source estimates and their dates remain unchanged. v13.10: the timeline cards keep their text and sizes in 75 mm (was 82).

p9.reason: The complete observation and memory model stays in the right column at its existing type sizes.

p10.reason: The full token-family table stays in the right column at its existing 193.5 by 118 mm size. v13.10: one 17 pt line states what the token family is for agents; the table and caption are unchanged.

p11.reason: The SAT-042 execution strip prints the existing reference-harness run, its three refusals, chained trace and anchor scores. The headline concerns the reported run; no spacecraft deployment is claimed.

v13.2_notes.what: SAT-042 placed as panel 11 (compact strip F15b); the right column rows are in the brief section B 'v13.2 change' table, so p7 to p11 need no deviation entry
departures_from_the_plan: F8 ladder drawn at 60 mm, not about 110: panels 8 to 10 keep 428 mm with their figures, so panel 7 and panel 11 share 199 mm; the kicker of panel 11 alone takes two lines at 24 pt (200 mm of text in a 193.5 mm column)
F15b strip 60 mm, not 70: its three rows end at 60 mm at 14 pt; the 10 mm were needed for the column

panel 7 prints no mechanism line ('Each rung names what it still trusts.' would be false without the trust lines) and no caption (the rungs print the counts; the threat model and the conclusion carry the entity, sensor and decision scope)
panel 11 headline at 28 pt, one line (32 pt wraps to two: 198 mm)
the ladder's 'still trusted' lines and the 409 are not printed (one evidence line per rung)

v13.9_notes.reason: The complete seven-step workflow is read before the controlled handoff experiment; panel 11 now carries the compact SAT-042 execution-verification strip instead of a next-experiments prose block.

v13.10_notes.what: Recovered from the v10 board (5143fac): the lead question and answer (header, beside the hero), the memory-as-coded box (centre, after panel 4, streamlined to seven rows) and the full trace (left, after panel 7, condensed; the ten-client-path sentence is left out because panel 12 prints the later 11-path measurement). Column gaps: left 4, centre 1, right 3 mm. The header image strip states the scene-to-token reduction instead of the location credit, which panels 1, 2 and 4 already carry. The 'Hand off' workflow step carries the strongest fill.
v13.10_notes.variants: Two print variants from one source (build_v13.py --variant): 0of300 (default) prints false acceptance as pre-registered; 300of300 prints the complement as 'did not act on' with the declined / genuine split. Only panel 1's outcome column and take line and panel 5's agent bars, totals and bar note differ.
v13.10_notes.eo_review: Response to the EO reviewer's report of 4 Oct 2026: research/v13/26_V13_10_REVIEW.md section 10.
v13.10_notes.title: 4 Oct 2026, authors' choice: the printed title is the programme title up to 'Protocol', on one line. The header re-spaces the freed line: title down 3 mm; hero and lead up 13.8 mm, subhero up 10.4 mm, bridge up 7.9 mm; the byline keeps the bottom edge (ink gaps title-hero 15, hero-subhero 6, subhero-bridge 8, bridge-byline 13 mm).
v13.10_notes.versions: No service or code commit on the face (footer, memory-as-coded label, panel 10 note): versions advance with every upgrade. The rows K.commit and CODE.commit keep them; face_hygiene fails on a commit hash.

(the figure counts false acceptance); one name for the condition (emem reference); panel 5 checks carry their layers (the L0 to L3 key); f6 names its deterministic row; the header orbit line is a design goal; the subhero adds the signed absence. research/v13/26_V13_10_REVIEW.md section 13.

v13.10_notes.two_reviews: 4 Oct 2026: fixes from the ChatGPT and cold-read reviews (review log section 15). The source-pixel panel moves above the mutation matrix and is numbered 5; L0 to L3 text leaves the face (depth shows as colour and check names).
v13.10_notes.deliberate_cut: 4 Oct 2026, after the second ChatGPT review: panel 3 drops the drift-score figure and its caption; panel 11 drops the score values (undefined without it); the code box keeps the fact, name and cell rows (recall, signing, log and receipt are in panels 8 and 4 and the trace) and is titled 'The record, as coded'; panel 6 and panel 9 drop a sentence each that repeated other text. The space goes to panel 7's table (17 pt), the full trace (17 pt, from 14), the token table (8 mm rows, from 6.7) and air between panels. Words on the face 3,255 to 3,043; at 14 pt 1,695 to 1,348.
v13.10_notes.relay_box: 4 Oct 2026: panel 1's relay box prints one wrapped list of the R5 change families under 'relay or faulty signer' and 'one change per trial, shared corruption families' (was 'same set on each lane', which read as equal item sets; the sets are 23, 24 and 25 items); no family sits beside a lane. Review log sections 18 and 19.
v13.10_notes.matched_baseline: 4 Oct 2026: panel 1's scope prints the pre-registered matched baseline (research/repro/v13/r5/prereg_addendum2.md, pushed before it was computed): 'Matched baseline (4 Oct): emem's checks minus hash, signature and log, run on the JSON, accepted 8 of 23 corruptions (3 with four more checks; emem's verifier 0); in an exploratory run, one trial each, instructed Haiku agents given those checks acted on the same 8.' It replaced 'no equal-tool baseline yet'. To give the scope a fifth line, f2's lane gaps went from 3.0 to 1.6 mm (figure 118 to 112.5 mm, lane height unchanged) and the spine-foot margin from 1.6 to 0.6 mm. Review log sections 19 and 20.
v13.10_notes.third_review: 4 Oct 2026: ChatGPT review of a8ad558, 8.2/10. Its one wording fix (relay box 'same set on each lane' implied equal item sets; they are 23, 24 and 25) is applied as 'shared corruption families'. Its main open point, the matched baseline, is run and printed. Review log section 19; the audit that followed is section 20.
v13.10_notes.ablation_strip: 4 Oct 2026 (fourth ChatGPT review): the matched ablation is its own labelled strip under the handoff figure, 17 pt on a grey ground with an emem rule: 'Matched ablation, deterministic receiver, same 23 corruptions (4 Oct), accepted: JSON, no checks 23 -> emem's checks minus hash, signature and log 8 -> plus four consistency checks 3 -> emem's verifier 0'. The scope keeps the exploratory agent run and returns to four lines. Panel 1's gaps above the mechanism line (1.0 to 0.6 mm) and the figure (1.6 to 0.8 mm) give the strip its 7 mm. Review log section 21.
v13.10_notes.footer_dates: 4 Oct 2026: 'Measurements: 29 Sep to 4 Oct 2026.' (row K.dates). Review log section 21.
v13.10_notes.brand: 4 Oct 2026, authors' identity: the emem wordmark (em, a drawn orange dash, em) sits at the header's bottom right, 52 pt Bold white, right edge on the text column (620 mm), baseline on the byline's second baseline (182.7 mm). The dash is a CSS bar (0.9 em by 0.12 em at mid x-height), not a character, because the face bans the em dash. The bridge prints the card tagline as the design goal, 'Design goal: encode in orbit, decode with AI.', with 'decode with AI.' in the brand orange (token brand #E86424). The byline moves up 1.5 mm (top 169.5 mm) so the wordmark's glyph box ends inside the 188 mm block; the bridge-byline ink gap goes from 13 to 11.5 mm. The brand orange marks identity on the navy header and is never used for data. Review log section 22.
